# Report - video43 (L1 proxy, Three.js sampled-frame baseline)

Representation level: L1 (proxy). Three.js sampled-frame baseline; not a Blender-protocol reproduction.

Observed (24 reference samples, 0-4.88 s): one continuous shot, 2.40:1 letterboxed. A camera high above a two-lane desert highway (yellow left edge line, dashed centre line, white right edge line, rumble-strip shoulders, gravel, desert with green shrubs) starts looking steeply down at the road, holds briefly, then tilts up smoothly, easing out to a near-level sunset view (sun upper right, dark cloud band, mountain silhouettes on the right). A yellow/white van enters from the bottom right (passing under the camera) at ~0.2 s and drives away in the right lane; a white car ahead in the left lane appears at the top at ~1.0 s and pulls away; a far truck sits near the vanishing point; a far-left opposite carriageway carries a white semi (visible at the left edge ~1.3-2.1 s) and oncoming cars with headlights.

Geometry: ground built from long vertex-coloured strips (lanes, lines, shoulders, rumble strips, gravel, desert, far road), dashed centre line as quads with 12.2 m period, instanced flattened spheres for shrubs, cones for mountains, procedural shader sky dome with sun glow and cloud band, fog for haze. Van proxy = yellow lower box + white upper box + window/taillight/bumper boxes + 4 rolling wheels. Cars/trucks = simple box combinations with rolling wheels.

Camera (inferred): fixed position 8.7 m above the road, ~0.25 m left of the centre line; vertical FOV ~19.5 deg (f ~2100 px at 720 p). Pitch keyframed per sample from the observed horizon/vanishing-line position (about 21 deg down at start to ~0.5 deg down at end) with monotone cubic interpolation; slight yaw so the road vanishing point sits left of centre. Letterbox via camera-attached black bars.

Timing (inferred from sample geometry): van rear distance ~12.8 m at 0.21 s, ~27 m at 0.83 s, then ~25.4 m/s; white car ~35 m/s; oncoming vehicles ~30 m/s.

Render feedback: none received yet (initial round). All distances, focal length and speeds are estimates from single-image measurements and are unverified.
